criteria.text: The response identifies that APA Section 1.3(c) defines Assumed Liabilities to include product liability claims for Products manufactured or sold before Closing. It also identifies that Buyer's indemnity for Assumed Liabilities (Section 9.3(b)) is excluded from any cap or limitation (Section 9.5(c)). Together these leave Muvux with uncapped exposure for pre-closing product liability. The response notes that this departs from the LOI, under which that liability stayed with Seller. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.
hints: whether manufactured or sold before or after the Closing

criteria.text: The response identifies that Seller Note Section 6(e) makes a Change of Control of any Person controlling Maker an Event of Default absent Holder's prior written consent. It states that the parent's August 27, 2026 merger with Ardentis, disclosed in APA Section 5.5, would trigger that default. It notes that no consent from Pisen has been obtained. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.

The response identifies that Seller Note Section 8(b) subjects claims for Excluded Liabilities under APA Section 9.2(c) to the Seller Indemnity Cap, overriding the carve-out in APA Section 9.5(b). It states that APA Section 11.9 gives the Seller Note precedence over the APA, so the Note's provision governs. It explains why this matters to the client and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Purchase Price is $68,000,000, consisting of $54,000,000 cash at Closing and a $14,000,000 Seller Note.
The response states that the Seller Indemnity Cap is 12% of the Purchase Price, or $8,160,000.
The response presents the issues in an order or ranking that it expressly identifies as reflecting their significance to the client.
The response includes a section or statements flagging matters it could not resolve from the documents alone. For each one, it identifies the information needed to resolve it.
The response claims that the LOI's allocation of pre-closing product liability to Seller is binding and controls over the APA's definition of Assumed Liabilities.
The response claims that Muvux's indemnity claims for Excluded Liabilities remain uncapped because APA Section 9.5(b) prevails over Seller Note Section 8(b).
